FEATURE / REFERENCE-DRIVEN WORLDBUILDER ISSUE: Extend `WorldbuildingGalleryShowcase` with a dedicated town-architecture showcase derived from the original Mounting Force town screenshots that were added under `References/MountingForce/map-images/`.

REFERENCE SOURCE: Treat the complete screenshot set for each town prefix as the visual source, not just the outdoor overview. Inspect the town overview plus its houses, shops, church/civic spaces, caves/underground spaces, and other interiors where present:
- Kentridge: `kentridge*.png`
- Hightown: `hightown*.png`
- Moordell: `moordell*.png`
- Rossdam: `rossdam*.png`
- Fairy Village: `fairy-village*.png`
- Orc Village: `orc-village*.png`

The goal is not a literal tile-for-tile remake. Reinterpret the original themes as high-quality 3D voxel architecture while preserving each town's recognizable architectural language, material family, color story, building roles, and environmental character. The towns must feel related to the original screenshots, but the result should look like a deliberate modern voxel-world art direction rather than enlarged pixel art.

PROPOSED TOWN ART DIRECTIONS (refine these after directly inspecting the screenshots; screenshot evidence wins when it conflicts with these starting points):

KENTRIDGE — pastoral, practical human village.
Materials/colors: warm fieldstone foundations and wells; cream/tan plaster; exposed medium-to-dark timber framing; weathered oak doors/beams; thatch and/or muted wood-shingle roofs; moss/grass greens; restrained faded red, blue, or ochre accents.
Structures: timber-framed cottages, inn/pub, church, mayor/large residence, weapon/armor/magic shop variants, warehouse/storehouse, village well, fences, carts, porches, sheds, stone paths and small retaining walls. The well should read as a recognizable Kentridge landmark.

HIGHTOWN — more established, elevated, civic/religious and prosperous.
Materials/colors: dressed pale or gray stone/ashlar; cleaner plaster; dark slate or refined shingle roofs; heavier carved timber; iron hardware/railings; stained-glass or colored-window accents; controlled burgundy/navy/royal-blue highlights.
Structures: taller multi-story townhouses, formal church, mayor/civic house, organized shopfronts, pub, arched passages, stone stairs/terraces, retaining walls, under-church/cellar/cave transition pieces, lamps and formal street details. Silhouettes should be taller, more vertical, and more orderly than Kentridge.

MOORDELL — rugged moorland settlement, weathered and grounded.
Materials/colors: dark weathered stone, rough fieldstone, peat/earth, heavy aged timber, slate and coarse thatch, moss/lichen, iron, desaturated brown/olive/gray with small heather-purple or warm amber accents.
Structures: low stone cottages, stout inn/pub, compact shops, grave/memorial element, rough boundary walls, stone steps, drainage/ditches, sheds, wind-worn fences, cellar/underground entrances. Forms should feel squat, durable, and adapted to harsh weather.

ROSSDAM — fortified/royal town with stronger civic hierarchy.
Materials/colors: cut stone and masonry, optionally warm brick/sandstone where supported by the screenshots; dark structural timber; slate or clay-tile roofing; iron and brass; cleaner paving; crimson, royal blue, deep green, and restrained gold accents for banners/trim.
Structures: fortified gate/wall vocabulary, formal residences, king/chamber or hall vocabulary, weapon/armor/magic shop fronts, larger civic buildings, arches, towers, guard posts, plazas, banners and more deliberate street geometry. The district should communicate greater wealth and authority without becoming a generic castle kit.

FAIRY VILLAGE — whimsical organic settlement integrated with nature.
Materials/colors: pale/curved wood, bark, roots, moss, leaves, flowers, woven fibers, light stone, luminous crystal/glass accents, soft aqua/teal, leaf green, lilac/pink and warm golden light.
Structures: treehouses, hollow-trunk rooms, root/branch bridges, elevated platforms, curved stairs, cave-integrated rooms, tiny porches/balconies, organically shaped inn/pub and shops, lanterns/crystals, flower beds and oversized natural forms. Architecture should look grown around or out of vegetation, not human houses recolored green.

ORC VILLAGE — rough tribal/fortified settlement with a strong forge/war-camp character.
Materials/colors: dark stone/basalt, packed earth, rough-hewn logs, heavy planks, hide/leather, rope, bone/tusk accents, blackened iron, soot, olive/brown with smoky red/orange accents.
Structures: stockades, watchtowers, longhouse/feast-hall forms, rough huts, forge/weapon and armor stalls, magic/totem hut, pub/communal hall, training-yard pieces, gates, braziers, racks, spikes and heavy timber supports. It should feel handmade, massive and asymmetrical, not merely damaged human architecture.

SHOWCASE COMPOSITION:
Create one walkable gallery/showcase in `WorldbuildingGalleryShowcase` divided into six clearly separated town districts. Each district needs:
1. A readable town label/sign and a compact palette/material display showing its primary wall, roof, structural, ground, trim and accent materials.
2. Multiple architecture examples, not just swatches: at minimum one residential example, one commercial/shop example, one civic/communal example, and one landmark/infrastructure example appropriate to that town.
3. Characteristic street/ground treatment and a small set of town-specific exterior props/landscape details so the materials can be judged in context.
4. Enough spacing and sightline separation that a viewer can immediately compare the six architectural languages without them visually bleeding together.
5. Consistent enough neutral lighting that material/color differences are real and not created only by different lighting. Town-specific emissives, lanterns, foliage, fog, etc. may supplement the identity but must not be the sole source of differentiation.

Do not solve the gallery by cloning one generic cottage/shop six times and recoloring it. Each town needs distinct roof shapes, wall construction, proportions, trim, openings, support details, silhouettes, verticality, density, and prop language. Buildings must meet the repository AAA world-authoring bar: believable construction, readable entrances/windows/roofs/supports, coherent scale, grounded placement, clear circulation, no floating pieces, and no unintended intersections.

ARCHITECTURE BOUNDARY: The six town style definitions, material palettes, reusable building/structure programs, and gallery composition must be expressed through the standard WorldBuilder/shared world-authoring APIs and shared material/assembly systems. `WorldbuildingGalleryShowcase` may select town styles, seeds, dimensions and layout intent, but it must not own bespoke direct voxel-writing, procedural mesh code, or one-off hand-authored building geometry. Do not hand-build the showcase directly in the `.unity` hierarchy. If the shared WorldBuilder cannot express a required roof, timber frame, treehouse/root bridge, stockade, civic facade, material family, palette, signage, or other reusable concept, generalize that capability in the shared engine/worldbuilding layer and expose it through WorldBuilder.

ACCEPTANCE:
(1) The built `WorldbuildingGalleryShowcase` contains six clearly labeled, walkable districts: Kentridge, Hightown, Moordell, Rossdam, Fairy Village, and Orc Village.
(2) Every district is visibly grounded in its corresponding `References/MountingForce/map-images/<town-prefix>*.png` source set; implementation evidence identifies which screenshots drove the selected forms/materials.
(3) Every district presents a readable material/color palette in both swatch form and on actual architecture.
(4) Every district contains at least the required residential, commercial, civic/communal, and landmark/infrastructure examples, using town-specific structural language rather than recolored clones.
(5) The six districts are visually distinct at a glance in silhouette, construction, palette and prop/environment language while still belonging to one coherent voxel-game art direction.
(6) All new theme/material/building capabilities are reusable WorldBuilder/shared-system concepts; scene code only composes them.
(7) Focused behavioral regressions exercise the production WorldBuilder path and prove that all six town programs resolve to their intended material families and required structure roles.
(8) The exact built-application `WorldbuildingGalleryShowcase` harness reaches a usable rendered scene without startup/runtime exceptions and captures evidence of all six districts.
(9) Review the rendered result directly against the original screenshots and the AAA world-authoring bar; semantic counts alone are insufficient.
(10) Check blast radius, world-build cost, material/shader cost, draw/triangle impact, and memory impact for any new shared primitive or material system; do not weaken existing device budgets.
